first.rationale: The two live symptoms (onboarding completion -4% QoQ, activation -6% QoQ) point at the funnel stage that memory_86 and memory_31 both address, and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing it can move both. I deliberately do not chase the competitor with promotional_pricing: memory_73 reports acquisition and revenue lift, but discount-acquired SMB cohorts are the classic case where short-horizon lift and long-horizon qualified revenue diverge, and the summary carries no retention or expansion horizon. Referral (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) are healthy but address neither declining metric this week. I spend both verification pulls on the memories I actually intend to act on rather than on the one I intend to decline. memory_31 is the priority pull because the consolidated line hides the key downstream hazard: cutting required signup fields raises activation partly by admitting less-qualified accounts and by destroying the qualification data that routes and scores them, so the measured 'durable lift in first-week activation' may be a proxy win that does not carry through to qualified revenue. I want the original record's segment definition, horizon, and whether any revenue-quality metric was tracked at all. memory_86 is the second pull to check whether 'shortening onboarding' meant removing friction or removing setup steps that drive real time-to-value, and whether its cohort overlaps memory_31's such that the two are one effect double-counted. Both memories are also stale relative to the current competitive environment (day 12 and day 52 vs. day 76 with a new entrant), so prior effect sizes are upper bounds, not forecasts. Hence a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout: hold out a control, keep any removed signup fields as optional or post-signup progressive capture so qualification data is not lost, and gate on qualified-pipeline and 30/60-day retention rather than on completion and activation alone. If verification shows memory_31's lift was measured only on activation with no revenue-quality follow-through, I shift the slot's emphasis toward activation_messaging (memory_91), which improves engagement without altering who gets in the door.

final.rationale: Verification resolved the question I cared about and it split the two memories rather than confirming them equally. exp_86 (shortened onboarding) is the clean one: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and critically 30-day retention +3% — the downstream indicator moved the same direction as the proxy, which is exactly the pattern that makes a proxy trustworthy. exp_31 (signup simplification) is weaker than its consolidated summary implied: the headline signup +15% and activation +9% shrink to qualified revenue +4% with retention -1%, i.e. roughly two-thirds of the funnel lift did not survive to revenue, and it is explicitly SMB-only and not replicated elsewhere. That is the admission-quality leak I suspected. So I take the onboarding-flow intervention (exp_86 shape: reduce steps and time-to-value inside the flow) and I do NOT take the signup-field-cutting intervention (exp_31 shape) — they were being conflated under one banner, and only one of them earns the slot. This directly addresses onboarding completion -4% and, because onboarding sits upstream, should partially relieve activation -6% without changing who is admitted. I still decline promotional_pricing against the competitor: memory_73 remains unverified, discount-acquired SMB is precisely the cohort where measured lift decays, and I would be spending the slot on the one direction whose downstream evidence I never checked. Residual uncertainty I am not papering over: exp_86 never measured qualified revenue directly, only retention as a 30-day proxy; it is day-52 evidence in a day-76 market with a new entrant, so the +13%/+3% figures are ceilings not forecasts; and shortening onboarding under competitive pressure can tempt removal of setup steps that actually produce value, which would invert the effect. Therefore standard experiment with a real holdout, not a broad rollout: cut sequencing and friction, preserve every step that drives first meaningful action, instrument 30/60-day retention and qualified pipeline as the decision gates rather than completion rate, and pre-commit to killing it if completion rises while retention flattens. If it lands, activation_messaging (memory_91) is the natural next slot since it compounds on the same funnel stage.
